learning.why: teacher explained with pizza slice comparison—slice with two straight edges is sector (trijyas), straight cut across is segment (chord); board drawing showing trijya+chap vs jeeva+chap made it click

end.summary:
Identified radius, chord, diameter, arc, segment and sector, including a new-situation question; the sector/segment mix-up was corrected later.
Related diameter, radius and chord lengths in several examples; this remains partly checked.
Practised reflection and rotation symmetry, but the circle’s number of symmetry lines was still given as four.
Teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Asha practised circle parts, chord and diameter relationships, and reflection and rotation symmetry with Dev. Dev used the centre-to-rim idea to distinguish radii and the centre-crossing idea to distinguish diameters; the sector/segment mix-up was corrected later in the lesson. The circle’s symmetry was still described as having four lines, so next time Asha can revisit that with a tracing-paper turn and several different fold lines. At home, ask Dev to draw a circle and test whether a line through any two opposite points leaves both halves matching.
